name: Selaginellaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Selaginella as a lycophyte rather than a fern: tiny single-veined ligulate microphylls on branching shoots, rhizophores, terminal strobili, and heterospory with a few large megaspores plus hundreds of tiny microspores.

project_scope.selection_mode: Selaginella apoda + Selaginella arenicola project module
project_scope.note: Both species are accepted by current Kew and native ranges include Texas. S. arenicola has two accepted subspecies; species-level subspecies resolution remains separate.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Use magnification on a leafy shoot. Each tiny leaf is a single-veined microphyll with a small ligule near the adaxial base. Look also for leafless rhizophores descending from stems/branch forks.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Small terrestrial or rock-growing vascular plants with dichotomously or irregularly branched leafy stems. Leaves are tiny, single-veined and ligulate; they may be all similar or dimorphic and arranged in four ranks.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Sporophylls form terminal strobili. A single sporangium sits in the axil of each sporophyll.
family_diagnostics.spores: Heterosporous: megasporangia contain usually four very large megaspores, while microsporangia contain hundreds of tiny microspores.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Tiny leafy branching vascular plant + ligule + rhizophore + two spore sizes = Selaginellaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole shoot → microphyll + ligule → rhizophore → strobilus → mega-vs-microsporangium → mega-vs-microspore → apoda vs arenicola → true-fern comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Spikemoss looks mossy, but it is a vascular lycophyte. Its most important visual ideas are tiny microphylls, specialized rhizophores, and two dramatically different spore sizes.

steps.title: 1 · Prove it is a leafy vascular shoot
steps.look_for: Branching stem densely covered with tiny leaves rather than a fern frond or moss gametophyte.
steps.why_it_matters: Sets the body plan before magnification.

steps.title: 2 · Find the ligule
steps.look_for: A minute membranous ligule on the upper/adaxial surface near the base of each single-veined microphyll.
steps.why_it_matters: The ligule is a core Selaginellaceae character and separates spikemoss from many lookalikes.

steps.title: 3 · Find a rhizophore
steps.look_for: A leafless root-bearing axis emerging from the stem or branch fork and producing roots at its tip.

steps.title: 4 · Open the strobilus
steps.look_for: Overlapping sporophylls forming a terminal strobilus, each with one sporangium at its base.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the leafy shoot to lycophyte reproduction.

steps.title: 5 · Put megaspores beside microspores
steps.look_for: A megasporangium with only a few very large megaspores versus a microsporangium packed with hundreds of minute microspores.
steps.why_it_matters: Heterospory is the family concept learners are most likely to remember visually.

steps.title: 6 · Selaginella apoda door
steps.look_for: Delicate prostrate/short-creeping mat, dorsiventrally flattened branches, dimorphic leaves in four ranks, and lax flattened strobili; typically moist habitats.
steps.why_it_matters: Contrasts a soft wet-site species with the dry-site radial architecture of S. arenicola.

steps.title: 7 · Selaginella arenicola door
steps.look_for: Erect/ascending clumping shoots that are radially symmetric, with narrow appressed leaves in pseudowhorls of four and bristle tips; dry sandy, gravelly or rock habitat.
steps.why_it_matters: The growth form and leaf arrangement are strong project-level contrasts with S. apoda.

steps.title: 8 · Compare with Joey's Adiantum
steps.look_for: Adiantum has a true fern frond bearing sori along the blade margin; Selaginella has microphyll-covered stems and terminal heterosporous strobili.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the fern-versus-lycophyte split visually concrete using authoritative private-study footage.

comparisons.title: Selaginellaceae vs Equisetaceae
comparisons.rule: Selaginella has individual ligulate microphylls, rhizophores and heterosporous strobili. Equisetum has jointed hollow ribbed stems, leaves fused into nodal sheaths, and homosporous terminal strobili.

comparisons.title: Selaginellaceae vs true ferns
comparisons.rule: Selaginella is a lycophyte with microphylls and terminal strobili; true ferns such as Adiantum make fronds and bear sporangia in sori on the blade or specialized fern structures.

comparisons.title: S. apoda vs S. arenicola
comparisons.rule: S. apoda is delicate, prostrate/short-creeping, flattened and usually moisture-loving with dimorphic 4-ranked leaves. S. arenicola forms erect/ascending radially symmetric dry-site shoots with narrow appressed leaves and bristle tips.

visual_lesson.caveat: The ligule is tiny and may require magnification. Do not identify Selaginella from a vague 'mossy' appearance; confirm vascular-shoot architecture, microphyll arrangement, rhizophores and/or strobili.

genera.fast_cue: tiny ligulate microphylls + rhizophores + terminal heterosporous strobili

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; native range includes Texas.
